metadata.title: China and global benchmark electricity-only AI compute cost curves
metadata.notes: The observation cutoff governs displayed values. The research publication cutoff is a provenance freeze and does not change an observation's date.

capacityStandard.label: Commissioned design IT power
capacityStandard.definition: Non-redundant IT or critical-load power that commissioned data-center space is designed to support, excluding cooling and other facility overhead.
capacityStandard.chinaBoundary: Design rack capacity in commissioned computing centers, converted at 2.5 kW per standard rack.
capacityStandard.globalBoundary: Operational or commissioned maximum rated IT power. The US register uses JLL year-end 2025 leased plus hyperscaler-owned capacity across ten leading markets; Great Britain covers official regional colocation estimates; India covers seven primary live-IT markets.
capacityStandard.coverageCaveat: Capacity coverage and price coverage are reported separately. The 62 GW global denominator is indicative because its published boundary is not documented at the same regional detail as the register.

treemap.measurementMethod: Rectangle edges were recorded in pixels from a 160 dpi render. Capacity equals rectangle area divided by the complete treemap area, multiplied by 10.43 million standard racks and 2.5 kW per rack. The 31 rectangles exactly tile the recorded outer bounds.

evidenceScenarios.title: Strict data-center-specific subset
evidenceScenarios.subtitle: Delivered data-center price or demonstrably applicable large-load tariff
evidenceScenarios.note: Audit-only subset using Hohhot's reported delivered green-power price and Hydro-Québec Rate LG. It remains in the coverage table but is folded into the combined price-evidence category for the public cost curves.

evidenceScenarios.title: Observed prices or applicable tariffs
evidenceScenarios.subtitle: One combined category, with the evidence type retained on every block
evidenceScenarios.note: Combines applicable public large-load tariffs and official 2025 industrial averages. US blocks use EIA state industrial averages rather than disclosed data-center contracts; Pacific Northwest and Omaha remain registered but unpriced because their market boundaries cross states. Hohhot's delivered-price observation remains in the strict audit subset because its capacity is nested inside the Inner Mongolia provincial width and cannot be added without double counting.

chinaCapacityCrosschecks.capacityBoundary: In-use standard racks across the province.
chinaCapacityCrosschecks.note: This is the closest-date direct provincial observation found. It is materially below the CAICT area-implied March estimate, so the disagreement is exposed rather than resolved by silently choosing one source.

chinaCapacityCrosschecks.capacityBoundary: In-use standard racks in computing centres across the province.
chinaCapacityCrosschecks.note: A later same-year observation. It is useful for showing growth and for checking plausibility, but it is not a March replacement.

chinaCapacityCrosschecks.capacityBoundary: Province-wide in-use standard racks; the source says the total exceeded 350,000.
chinaCapacityCrosschecks.note: The direct source supplies a lower bound, not a point estimate. The CAICT area-implied figure clears that bound.
This later direct observation is close to the CAICT area-implied March estimate and is retained as corroboration.

chinaCapacityCrosschecks.capacityBoundary: Province-wide in-use standard racks in MIIT's 2025 computing-power monitoring data.
chinaCapacityCrosschecks.note: A direct year-end observation from the national monitoring system. It is not substituted into the March distribution because China-wide rack capacity also grew substantially during 2025.
A direct year-end figure published on a Guangdong government site; the underlying provincial table is not linked.

chinaCapacityCrosschecks.capacityBoundary: Province-wide design capacity of in-use data centres, expressed as standard racks.
chinaCapacityCrosschecks.note: The boundary closely matches CAICT's definition and the direct value is close to the area-implied March 2025 estimate, but the observation is one quarter earlier.

chinaCapacityCrosschecks.capacityBoundary: Province-wide in-use standard racks; Hubei Data Bureau data reported as more than 210,000.
chinaCapacityCrosschecks.note: The source supplies a later lower bound rather than an exact count.

chinaCapacityCrosschecks.capacityBoundary: Standard racks built by the province's information and communications industry.
chinaCapacityCrosschecks.note: The official statistical bulletin is direct and precise, but its industry scope may omit non-telecom facilities and its date is later than the CAICT distribution.

chinaCapacityCrosschecks.capacityBoundary: Standard racks across key data centres described jointly as under construction and in operation.
chinaCapacityCrosschecks.note: This is a province-wide official result, but it covers key centres and combines construction and operation. It is therefore not the same population as CAICT's in-use design-rack total.

chinaCapacityCrosschecks.capacityBoundary: Province-wide standard racks; the source does not state whether the count is in-use design capacity, built capacity or installed capacity.
chinaCapacityCrosschecks.note: An official current total that is useful for order-of-magnitude checking, but the missing in-use boundary and later date prevent substitution.

chinaCapacityCrosschecks.capacityBoundary: Municipality-wide in-use data-centre standard racks, attributed to the Shanghai Communications Administration.
chinaCapacityCrosschecks.note: The boundary matches closely, but the observation precedes CAICT by 18 months and cannot measure the March 2025 stock directly.

chinaCapacityCrosschecks.capacityBoundary: Standard-rack scale across 59 data centres in Pudong.
chinaCapacityCrosschecks.note: A direct lower-level subtotal. It cannot replace or be added to the Shanghai provincial total.

chinaCapacityCrosschecks.capacityBoundary: Data-centre standard racks reported for the cluster; commissioned-versus-built wording is not explicit.
chinaCapacityCrosschecks.note: A major Inner Mongolia cluster subtotal. It is useful for triangulation but cannot replace the autonomous-region total.

chinaCapacityCrosschecks.capacityBoundary: Built racks; the same source separately reports 170,000 actually used racks.
chinaCapacityCrosschecks.note: A second Inner Mongolia cluster subtotal. The difference between built and actually used racks is retained in the boundary note.

chinaCapacityCrosschecks.capacityBoundary: Operational standard racks; the source separately reports 500,000 built racks and a 66% rack-up rate.
chinaCapacityCrosschecks.note: A year-end operating subtotal for one Inner Mongolia cluster. Together with Hohhot / Helinger it supports the scale of the autonomous-region estimate, but dates and possible boundary differences still prevent substitution.

chinaCapacityCrosschecks.capacityBoundary: Powered-on standard racks, not commissioned design racks.
chinaCapacityCrosschecks.note: A directly observed major-cluster subtotal already in the exclusion ledger; it remains useful as a lower-bound cross-check.

sources.publisher: China Academy of Information and Communications Technology
sources.title: Comprehensive Computing Power Index Blue Book (2025)
sources.claim: Provincial distribution and top-ten order of in-use standard racks; the report says the top six each exceed 600,000 racks but does not publish the 31 numeric values.
sources.locator: PDF page 22 / report page 16, Figure 6 and surrounding text; Appendix 1 states unspecified data are through 2025-03-31 and lists the China Computing Power Platform, MIIT, CAICT, local policy documents, literature and public data; Appendix 3 defines in-use racks.
sources.verificationMethod: Downloaded and rendered the source PDF, recorded its SHA-256, and reconciled all 31 rectangles. The project assumes treemap area is proportional to rack count; this reproduces an estimate, not CAICT's unpublished row-level inputs.

sources.publisher: China Computing Power Platform / China Academy of Information and Communications Technology
sources.title: What you need to know about the China Computing Power Platform
sources.claim: The platform had connected ten provincial platforms by July 2025 and supports resource registration, analysis and monitoring; it had accumulated billions of monitoring records.
sources.locator: Sections describing provincial-platform access, Shanxi's resource-registration functions and the July 2025 operating statistics.
sources.verificationMethod: Checked the official platform description and searched the public platform and report materials for a downloadable 31-province rack table; none was linked in the reviewed materials.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology
sources.title: MIIT launches nationwide automated computing-resource monitoring
sources.claim: MIIT set an end-2026 target for automated monitoring of computing-resource data across all 31 provincial-level regions and major computing enterprises.
sources.locator: Paragraph beginning '《通知》提出，到2026年底'.
sources.verificationMethod: Checked the target date, 31-region scope and monitoring description on MIIT's official page. This supports the conclusion that a complete public automated-monitoring census was not yet established in early 2026; it does not prove that no internal provincial table exists.
